title: Five Years of Taliban Rule: Education and Resistance in Afghanistan
subtitle: As the regime marks five years in power, it faces both internal military challenges and a deepening crisis in the nation's classrooms.

summary.en: Afghanistan is approaching the five-year anniversary of the Taliban's return to power. While the regime maintains control, it faces new military challenges from armed groups and internal instability. Meanwhile, the country's education system is undergoing a radical transformation. Girls are largely banned from secondary and higher education. Boys' schools are also changing, with a new focus on religious studies over traditional subjects.
summary.zh: 阿富汗即將迎來塔利班重掌政權五週年。儘管該政權維持著統治，但正面臨來自武裝團體的軍事挑戰與內部不穩定。同時，該國的教育體系正經歷激烈的轉型。女孩基本上被禁止接受中等與高等教育。男孩學校的教學內容也在改變，重點從傳統學科轉向宗教研究。

paragraphs.en: Five years after the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan, the country is facing a period of significant change and instability. While the regime has maintained control since August 2021, it is now dealing with new military threats. According to Deutsche Welle (DW), the Taliban recently lost control of a district center in the northeastern province of Badakhshan. Although the loss was temporary, it was the first time the group had lost a district center since taking over the country. Reports from the region also indicate internal fighting among Taliban members and attacks on high-ranking officials.
paragraphs.zh: 在塔利班（Taliban）重掌阿富汗政權五年後，該國正面臨一段充滿重大變革與不穩定的時期。儘管該政權自二零二一年八月以來維持著統治，但目前正應對新的軍事威脅。根據德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導，塔利班近期失去了東北部巴達赫尚省（Badakhshan）一個地區中心。雖然這次失守是暫時的，但這是該組織自接管國家以來首次失去地區中心。來自該地區的報導也指出，塔利班成員內部出現了鬥爭，且針對高層官員的攻擊事件頻傳。

paragraphs.en: Beyond these military challenges, various armed groups are continuing their resistance. Former Afghan army general Sami Sadat has ordered military operations against the Taliban, and the National Resistance Front remains active. Former Afghan Interior Minister Mohammad Umer Daudzai told DW that both political and military opposition have taken shape as the five-year mark approaches. Experts warn that the Taliban’s strict governing style could lead to more conflict, potentially opening the door for proxy wars—conflicts where outside countries use local groups to fight on their behalf.
paragraphs.zh: 除了這些軍事挑戰外，多個武裝團體也持續進行抵抗。前阿富汗陸軍將領薩達特（Sami Sadat）已下令對塔利班採取軍事行動，而民族抵抗陣線（National Resistance Front）也依然活躍。前阿富汗內政部長道扎伊（Mohammad Umer Daudzai）向德國之聲表示，隨著五年期限將至，政治與軍事反對勢力皆已成形。專家警告，塔利班嚴格的統治風格可能導致更多衝突，並可能為代理人戰爭——即外部國家利用當地團體代為作戰的衝突——開啟大門。

paragraphs.en: While the security situation remains tense, the impact of Taliban rule on education has been equally severe. Afghanistan is currently the only country in the world where girls are officially banned from secondary and higher education. According to the BBC, the Taliban has barred girls over the age of 12 from school. Many women, who have been pushed out of most workplaces, say their lives have become unrecognizable. "Survival has become the priority," said Ela, a resident of Kabul, explaining that many people no longer have the energy to think about the future.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管安全局勢依然緊張，塔利班統治對教育的影響同樣嚴重。阿富汗目前是全球唯一正式禁止女性接受中等與高等教育的國家。根據英國廣播公司（BBC）報導，塔利班已禁止十二歲以上的女孩進入學校。許多被迫離開職場的女性表示，她們的生活已變得面目全非。居住在喀布爾（Kabul）的艾拉（Ela）表示：「生存已成為首要任務。」她解釋說，許多人已無力再去思考未來。

paragraphs.en: When asked about these restrictions, Taliban foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi told the BBC that it is incorrect to say everything is banned for women. He claimed that three million girls are attending schools and madrassas, which are religious centers focused on Islamic teachings. However, the United Nations reports that only 7% of women in Afghanistan are employed, as they have been banned from many fields of study and work. For many young women, the loss of education feels like the loss of their dreams. Shakiba, who finished her secondary education online, told the BBC that her goal of becoming a pilot now feels impossible.
paragraphs.zh: 當被問及這些限制時，塔利班外交部長穆塔基（Amir Khan Muttaqi）向英國廣播公司表示，稱一切都對女性設限是不正確的。他聲稱有三百萬名女孩正在學校與伊斯蘭宗教學校（madrassas）就讀。然而，聯合國報告指出，阿富汗僅有百分之七的女性有工作，因為她們已被禁止進入許多研究與工作領域。對許多年輕女性而言，失去受教權感覺就像失去了夢想。透過線上完成中學教育的夏基芭（Shakiba）告訴英國廣播公司，她想成為飛行員的目標現在看來已不可能實現。

paragraphs.en: It is not only girls who are affected by the changing education system. NPR reports that boys are also facing a serious crisis. While boys are still allowed to attend school, the quality and content of their education have changed significantly. Interviews with students across the country suggest that schools are focusing less on science, mathematics, and languages like English, and much more on religious instruction. Teachers are now expected to include religious messages in almost every subject, and there is growing pressure for students to follow strict rules regarding their appearance, such as wearing traditional clothing.
paragraphs.zh: 教育體系的改變不僅影響了女孩。美國國家公共廣播電台（NPR）報導指出，男孩也面臨嚴重的危機。雖然男孩仍被允許上學，但教育的品質與內容已發生重大變化。對全國學生的訪談顯示，學校正減少對科學、數學與英語等語言的教學，轉而大幅增加宗教課程。教師現在被要求在幾乎每一門學科中加入宗教訊息，且學生面臨越來越大的壓力，必須遵守關於外表的嚴格規定，例如穿著傳統服飾。

paragraphs.en: Many students told NPR that the classroom no longer feels like a place of learning. Hashmat Mubariz, a 19-year-old who once attended a public school that taught science and literature, said that the atmosphere has shifted. He noted that many families now believe that modern, secular education—education not based on religion—will no longer lead to a future career. This shift is especially strong in southern provinces like Helmand and Kandahar, where religious studies were already a priority before the Taliban returned.
paragraphs.zh: 許多學生告訴美國國家公共廣播電台，教室已不再感覺像是學習的地方。十九歲的哈什馬特·穆巴里茲（Hashmat Mubariz）曾就讀於教授科學與文學的公立學校，他表示校園氛圍已經改變。他指出，許多家庭現在認為，現代的世俗教育——即非基於宗教的教育——將不再能帶來未來的職業發展。這種轉變在赫爾曼德省（Helmand）與坎達哈省（Kandahar）等南部省份尤為強烈，因為在塔利班回歸之前，這些地區就已將宗教研究視為優先事項。

paragraphs.en: As the Taliban marks five years in power, the regime continues to claim that it has restored nationwide security. However, this claim is challenged by the rise of armed opposition and the ongoing activity of groups like the regional branch of the Islamic State. Furthermore, the regime remains largely unrecognized by the international community. As former acting Minister of Defense Shahmohammad Miakhel noted to DW, the current policies of the Taliban may create the very conditions that lead to more resistance and interference from neighboring countries.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著塔利班執政滿五年，該政權持續聲稱已恢復全國安全。然而，武裝反對勢力的興起以及伊斯蘭國（Islamic State）區域分支的持續活動，挑戰了這一說法。此外，該政權在很大程度上仍未獲得國際社會承認。正如前國防部代理部長米亞赫爾（Shahmohammad Miakhel）向德國之聲所指出的，塔利班目前的政策可能會創造出導致更多抵抗與鄰國干預的條件。

paragraphs.en: For the people of Afghanistan, the future remains uncertain. Whether it is the young women who have been barred from classrooms or the young men who feel their education is no longer preparing them for the modern world, the daily reality is one of hardship. As the country moves past the five-year anniversary of the Taliban takeover, the gap between the regime's promises and the lived experiences of its citizens continues to grow.
paragraphs.zh: 對於阿富汗人民而言，未來依然充滿不確定性。無論是被拒於教室門外的年輕女性，還是覺得教育已無法讓他們為現代世界做好準備的年輕男性，每日的現實生活皆是艱辛。隨著該國度過塔利班接管五週年，政權的承諾與公民的實際生活體驗之間的鴻溝持續擴大。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become clear, organized, or developed.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語常被誤解為單純的「拿走形狀」，這裡指計畫或局勢變得具體。文中：Former Afghan Interior Minister Mohammad Umer Daudzai told DW that both political and military opposition have taken shape as the five-year mark approaches.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To force someone to leave a place or organization.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 被迫離開、被排擠出（某個領域）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指女性被排除在職場之外，而非字面上的推擠。文中：Many women, who have been pushed out of most workplaces, say their lives have become unrecognizable.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To officially prevent someone from doing something or entering a place.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（酒吧或柵欄），這裡作動詞用，表示官方禁止。文中：According to the BBC, the Taliban has barred girls over the age of 12 from school.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To signify or represent a specific point in time or an anniversary.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 標誌著（某個時間點或里程碑）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（分數或記號），這裡作動詞，表示到達某個時間點。文中：As the Taliban marks five years in power, the regime continues to claim that it has restored nationwide security.

While the regime maintains control, it is now facing new military challenges from armed groups. Internal clashes and attacks on officials have also created instability. Meanwhile, the quality of education for both boys and girls has declined significantly. Experts warn that these pressures could lead to further conflict and proxy wars in the region.

quiz.question: What is unique about the Taliban's recent military loss in the Badakhshan province?

options.A: It was the first time they lost a major city to the National Resistance Front.
options.B: It marked the first time the group lost control of a district center since seizing power.
options.C: It resulted in the permanent removal of Taliban leadership from the northeastern region.
options.D: It was caused by internal fighting rather than an attack by an external armed group.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據文章第一段，文中明確提到這是自塔利班掌權以來，首次失去一個地區中心（district center），儘管該損失是暫時的。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未說明該地是主要城市，且未指明是誰發動攻擊。選項 C 錯誤，因為文章指出該損失是「暫時的」（temporary）。選項 D 錯誤，文章雖提到內部鬥爭，但並未將此特定戰術損失歸因於內部衝突。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might the Taliban's current education policies lead to long-term instability?

options.A: Because the international community has promised to fund secular schools if the Taliban changes its curriculum.
options.B: Because the focus on religious instruction is causing a shortage of religious leaders in the country.
options.C: Because the shift away from modern, secular subjects may leave the next generation unprepared for the modern global economy.
options.D: Because the Taliban is planning to replace all public schools with online learning platforms.

quiz.explanationZh: 根據文章第五、六段，學校課程大幅減少科學、數學與語言教學，並轉向宗教教育。學生與家長認為這種教育方式無法提供未來的職業發展。推論可知，當年輕一代缺乏現代技能，將導致國家在現代經濟中失去競爭力，進而加劇社會的不滿與動盪。選項 A、B、D 在文中皆無依據，屬於過度推論或錯誤訊息。

quiz.question: In the second paragraph, what does the phrase 'proxy wars' mean in the context of the Taliban's governing style?

options.A: Conflicts where foreign nations manipulate local factions to fight on their behalf.
options.B: A type of civil war fought exclusively between members of the same political party.
options.C: Military exercises conducted by the Taliban to test the loyalty of their own soldiers.
options.D: Diplomatic negotiations that fail to reach a peaceful agreement between neighboring countries.

quiz.explanationZh: 文章第二段明確解釋了 proxy wars 為「conflicts where outside countries use local groups to fight on their behalf」。這是一個政治學術語，意指代理人戰爭。選項 B、C、D 皆與此定義不符，且與文章提到的「外部干預」概念背道而馳。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the Taliban's five-year rule?

options.A: The Taliban has successfully unified the country and improved the quality of religious education.
options.B: The Taliban is facing growing military, social, and educational crises that contradict their claims of stability.
options.C: The international community has fully recognized the Taliban government due to their focus on traditional values.
options.D: The Afghan people are generally satisfied with the shift toward religious instruction in schools.

quiz.explanationZh: 整篇文章的核心在於對照塔利班宣稱的「國家安全與穩定」，與實際發生的軍事反抗、教育體系崩壞、女性權利剝奪及經濟困境。文章旨在指出塔利班的承諾與人民的真實生活體驗之間存在巨大鴻溝，且面臨多重危機。選項 A 與 D 與文中描述的「hardship」（艱難）與「crisis」（危機）相違背；選項 C 則與文中提到的「largely unrecognized」（大部分未被認可）事實相反。
